The Robert Bosch GmbH is looking forward to your application! '} {'title': 'Job Description', 'text': ' As part of our research team, you will work on cutting-edge solutions for the life sciences. We are offering a PhD position to develop a novel dielectrophoresis (DEP) chip for the analysis and sorting of single cells. 
Multi-omics analyses at the single-cell level offer crucial diagnostic insights into diseases. However, current automation technologies are often inefficient and expensive. Your project will focus on overcoming these limitations by developing an image-based DEP chip to automate the compartmentation, sample preparation, analysis, and sorting of single cells. This technology aims to enable high-throughput, gentle multi-omics analyses for universal sample types. You will develop and evaluate innovative concepts for semiconductor-based dielectrophoresis (DEP) chips, determining robust electrical, microfluidic, and thermal operating parameters. Furthermore, you will investigate the physical limits of chip miniaturization and explore feasible manufacturing routes compatible with Bosch’s CMOS technology. You will design and fabricate a functional demonstrator using semiconductor manufacturing processes and integrate it into a microfluidic system. Last but not least, you will characterize the prototype and perform a proof of concept for all operating modes using a representative bioassay with living cells in physiological media. jobs.title: PhD - Lab on Chip Sample Preparation for Next-Generation Molecular Diagnostics
jobs.description:
{'title': 'Company Description', 'text': ' At Bosch, we shape the future by inventing high-quality technologies and services that spark enthusiasm and enrich people’s lives. Our promise to our associates is rock-solid: we grow together, we enjoy our work, and we inspire each other. Join in and feel the difference. The Robert Bosch GmbH is looking forward to your application! '} {'title': 'Job Description', 'text': ' Join our innovative research team. We are looking for a motivated PhD candidate to develop a microfluidic sample-preparation unit operation, based on magnetic beads, enabling next-generation molecular diagnostics (MDx) workflows. Next-generation molecular diagnostics require robust and automated methods for isolating low-abundance biological targets - such as pathogens, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), and extracellular vesicles (EVs)-from complex samples. This PhD project aims to develop a scalable, cartridge-compatible platform for the controlled handling of functionalized magnetic particles throughout the complete sample-preparation workflow, including target capture, washing, transfer, resuspension, and release. The central objective is to establish a reusable microfluidic actuation module that interfaces seamlessly with disposable diagnostic cartridges. You will conduct targeted literature research on the manipulation of magnetic particles and develop multiphysics models (e.g., COMSOL) to optimize particle trajectories and fluid interactions. Furthermore, you will conceptually design and develop a reusable, cartridge-compatible microfluidic handling module that automates the entire target-molecule extraction process (capture, washing, transfer, and release). You will create functional prototypes and experimentally quantify system performance using key metrics such as target-molecule recovery, processing time, and reproducibility. Last but not least, you will translate your physical understanding and modeling results into rigorous design rules for integration into disposable diagnostics cartridges, delivering transferable models and prototypes for future product development. '} {'title': 'Qualifications', 'text': " Education: excellent master's degree in Biomedical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Applied Physics, Microsystems Engineering (MEMS), or a related field Experience and Knowledge: solid knowledge of microfluidics, fluid dynamics, and multiphysics simulation (e.g., COMSOL); practical experience in the design, prototyping, and testing of lab-on-a-chip systems; ideally, familiarity with handling magnetic particles, non-Newtonian fluids (such as blood), or sample preparation for molecular diagnostics (MDx) Personality and Working Practice: you work independently, plan your tasks carefully, and contribute with a high level of commitment and a strong hands-on mentality; you are able to communicate your research findings clearly and bridge the gap between theoretical simulation and physical prototyping, taking ownership of your work Enthusiasm: you are passionate about interdisciplinary scientific work at the intersection of physics, engineering, and biomedicine, approach complex tasks creatively and innovatively, and successfully translate them into practical applications Languages: very good written and spoken German and English "} {'title': 'Additional Information', 'text': ' https://www.bosch-ai.com

jobs.title: Microstructural Characterization and Mechanical Testing of 3D metal printed on Advanced PCB Surfaces
jobs.description: Bitte aktivieren Sie JavaScript, um alle Funktionen nutzen zu können. Vision to Products Welcome to Hahn-Schickard: The research center for innovative microsystems technology. With a team of over 300 employees, we transform ideas into cross-industry solutions - from conception to production at three locations in Baden-Württemberg. At our Freiburg site, the emphasis is on developing analytical solutions in microsystems technology, particularly for point-of-care diagnostics. At the Freiburg site, the focus is on analytical solutions, especially for point-of-care diagnostics. But we also research, develop and manufacture electrochemical energy systems, autonomous fluidic robots and 3D printing of electronics. For our Laboratory Automation division, we offer at Freiburg im Breisgau the following position (beginning from November 2026 or later ): Research Student Assistant / Master Thesis (m/f/x) Microstructural Characterization and Mechanical Testing of 3D metal printed on Advanced PCB Surfaces Your Tasks You will be part of a team working on multi-material 3D printing platform for microfluidic and microelectronics applications. Getting familiar with the StarJet technology and establishing suitable jetting modes and process conditions for a molten metal alloy. Producing solder deposits and joints using different StarJet process parameters. Systematically investigating the influence of process parameters on the resulting printed metal. Performing materials characterization of printed deposits and solder joints, and investigating the interaction between solder alloy and different PCB surfaces. Preparing metallographic cross-sections and performing microscopy and other available materials characterization techniques. Evaluating the bonding performance of the resulting solder joints using suitable mechanical testing methods. Evaluate and visualize experimental data. Your profile Bachelor’s degree (or currently enrolled in a Master’s program) in Materials Science, Materials Engineering, Microsystems Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field.
